reviews.question: If a product is good or meets people’s needs, they will buy it. Therefore, advertising is unnecessary and no more than entertainment. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
reviews.originalEssay:
There is an opinion that if a product meets consumers' needs, it will naturally be purchased, rendering advertising unnecessary and merely a form of entertainment. Others, however, believe that marketing plays a crucial role in business success. In my opinion, while product quality is fundamental, I completely disagree that advertising is redundant.
   On the one hand, a product’s ability to fulfill customers’ needs and maintain high quality standards is undeniably vital for its commercial success. When a product excels at meeting consumer expectations, it naturally generates positive word-of-mouth publicity, which is often considered more credible than traditional commercial advertising. Satisfied buyers frequently recommend reliable items to their peers, fostering organic brand loyalty. For example, many local businesses thrive almost exclusively on the basis of their exceptional product quality and word-of-mouth reputation, without investing heavily in large-scale advertising campaigns.
   On the other hand, the necessity of advertising cannot be completely dismissed. In today’s highly competitive landscape, with an ever-increasing number of products and services on the market, it is essential for companies to distinguish themselves from their competitors and make potential customers aware of their offerings. Advertising plays a pivotal role in achieving this by allowing businesses to reach a wider audience and establish a memorable brand identity to stay ahead of their rivals. This is clearly seen in how even leading global firms unfailingly invest in advertisements across multiple platforms to maintain their market presence. Ultimately, without advertising, even high-quality products cannot go far in the market, just as advertising alone cannot ensure long-term success without genuine quality.
   In conclusion, while top-tier product quality is crucial for building trust and organic growth, advertising remains an indispensable business tool rather than mere entertainment. A successful brand requires a balance of both high product standards and effective marketing strategies.
reviews.overall: Em đã viết đủ 297 từ, giữ rõ quan điểm không đồng ý và triển khai đúng hai đoạn Cô giao. Em giải thích được vì sao chất lượng tạo truyền miệng, đồng thời quảng cáo giúp sản phẩm được biết đến giữa nhiều lựa chọn; hai ví dụ cũng gắn với ý chính. Các câu nối và cấu trúc em dùng nhìn chung chính xác. Cô gợi ý em chỉnh câu “Others, however” ở mở bài vì đề chỉ nêu một nhận định, để phần giới thiệu bám câu hỏi hơn.

reviews.question:
Today, the high sales of popular consumer goods reflect the power of advertising and not the real needs of the society in which they are sold.
To what extent do you agree or disagree?
reviews.originalEssay:
There is an opinion that the high sales figures of popular consumer products are primarily a result of powerful advertising rather than genuine societal demand. While I agree that advertising significantly influences consumer behavior, I disagree with the claim that it completely overrides real needs, as advertisements mainly amplify pre-existing desires rather than creating them out of nothing.
    On the one hand, advertising undoubtedly plays a major role in tempting people into buying products they might not otherwise need. Modern advertising agencies almost always employ diverse marketing strategies, such as eye-catching graphics, engaging content, and celebrity endorsements, to sway consumers' purchasing decisions. A prime example of this is the dramatic rise in sales of smartphones and tablets, which can be largely attributed to the highly effective advertising campaigns of tech giants like Apple or Samsung. Through persuasive promotion, these corporations convince buyers to upgrade their devices frequently, even when their existing models are still fully functional.
   On the other hand, the view that advertising creates entirely artificial needs is flawed, because there must be some underlying need before a person decides to make a purchase. Instead of manufacturing new needs, advertising merely magnifies and reinforces pre-existing ones. For instance, the sharp increase in demand for cosmetic products, particularly among females, can be ascribed to existing societal concerns about whether physical appearance determines success and happiness. Advertisements capitalize on these concerns by constantly highlighting the benefits of beauty-enhancing products and raising public awareness of the wide range of options available on the market. Thus, advertisements do not generate new demands from scratch, but rather fulfill and intensify existing desires.
   In conclusion, although persuasive marketing strategies can tempt individuals to purchase non-essential items, high sales ultimately depend on real consumer needs. In my view, advertising serves to amplify and reinforce genuine human needs rather than replace them entirely.
reviews.overall: Em đã viết đúng hướng không đồng ý với nhận định tuyệt đối trong đề và triển khai đủ hai đoạn theo dàn ý Cô giao. Đoạn đầu giải thích sức tác động của quảng cáo bằng các chiến lược tiếp thị và ví dụ điện thoại; đoạn sau chỉ ra nhu cầu có sẵn qua ví dụ mỹ phẩm. Em dùng từ chỉ mức độ và câu bị động phù hợp. Cô chỉ gợi ý sửa “advertisements ... fulfill ... desires” vì sản phẩm mới đáp ứng nhu cầu, còn quảng cáo khuếch đại chúng.

reviews.question:
Research indicates that nowadays some consumers are much less influenced by advertising than in the past.
What are the reasons for this trend?
Do you think this is a positive or negative development?
reviews.originalEssay:
It is true that consumers today are becoming increasingly resistant to advertising compared to the past. There are several key reasons for this trend, mainly stemming from advertising overload, and I believe this is a highly positive development for both consumers and businesses.
   The primary reason why people are increasingly indifferent to advertisements is their overwhelming presence in daily life. Today, consumers are constantly bombarded with commercial messages across virtually all platforms. On social media networks like YouTube, most viewers immediately click "skip after a few required seconds, while users on Facebook or TikTok often scroll past sponsored posts without paying any attention. Furthermore, a growing number of individuals actively install ad-blocking software to avoid being disturbed by intrusive pop-ups. As a consequence, many people have reported that they now rely more on online reviews, star ratings, and personal recommendations rather than on glossy commercials when making purchasing decisions.
   In my opinion, this change in consumer behavior represents a positive shift for both shoppers and companies. Firstly, consumers are now less likely to be manipulated by emotional or exaggerated messages in advertisements. Instead, they rely on careful comparisons, customer reviews, and their actual needs before making a purchase, which leads to a more intelligent and responsible form of consumption. Secondly, from the perspective of companies, this trend forces them to invest more in product quality, customer service, and innovation rather than relying solely on aggressive marketing. In the long run, both businesses and consumers benefit from a market driven by genuine value.
   In conclusion, the declining impact of advertising is largely driven by its omnipresence and the shift toward user-generated content. I view this as a welcome development, as it promotes smarter spending habits among consumers and encourages businesses to focus on real product quality.

reviews.question:
Online shopping is increasing dramatically.
How could this trend affect our environment and the kinds of jobs required?
reviews.originalEssay:
There is an opinion that the dramatic increase in online shopping can have significant effects on the environment and the types of jobs required in the future. From my perspective, this development has both positive and negative impacts.
    On the one hand, the growth of online shopping can have both positive and negative impacts on the environment. The rapid expansion of delivery services has resulted in the use of an increasingly large amount of plastic packaging. Consequently, numerous landfills have become filled with non-biodegradable waste, which can pose several health risks to species living on Earth. However, online shopping can also contribute positively to the environment by reducing the need for people to travel to physical stores. This may lower the number of vehicles on the roads, reducing fuel consumption and greenhouse gas emissions.
    On the other hand, the rise of online shopping is clearly transforming the job market. Many online platforms now use automated systems to process orders, handle payments and provide customer support. This may reduce the need for traditional retail jobs, such as cashiers and sales assistants, making it increasingly difficult for people without higher education or technical skills to find employment. Nevertheless, this transformation also creates new job opportunities. For instance, the expansion of e-commerce has increased demand for website developers, delivery workers, customer service staff and online marketing specialists. These jobs can provide new opportunities for people with appropriate digital skills.
    Overall, the rapid growth of online shopping can bring both advantages and disadvantages. While it may increase packaging waste and reduce some traditional retail jobs, it can also decrease transportation-related pollution and create new employment opportunities in the digital economy.

reviews.question:
Some say that news has no connection with most people's lives, and it is a waste of time for most of us to read newspapers and watch television news programs.
To what extent do you agree or disagree?
reviews.originalEssay:
There is an opinion that news has no connection with most people’s lives and that reading newspapers or watching television news programmes is a waste of time. From my perspective, there are some situations in which news may seem irrelevant, but I largely disagree with this statement.
    On the one hand, most news is related to people’s lives on a certain level, even when an event happens in another country. For example, the 2020 US presidential election might have seemed unrelated to Vietnamese people at first. However, changes in US leadership could influence international policies, trade and relations with other countries. In addition, developments involving China and the United States can affect the wider Southeast Asian region. Issues in the South China Sea are also relevant to Vietnam because the country has important economic and security interests in this area. Therefore, it is unreasonable to claim that news is fundamentally disconnected from people’s lives.
    On the other hand, it is also wrong to say that people essentially waste their time reading newspapers or watching news programmes. These activities can help alert the public to existing and potential problems in their communities. For instance, news about severe weather, traffic problems or public health issues can help people take appropriate precautions and make better decisions. Furthermore, following reliable news sources can help individuals understand important social and economic changes rather than remaining unaware of what is happening around them.
    Overall, although some news stories may appear unrelated to people’s daily lives, news can still influence individuals directly or indirectly. Therefore, I disagree with the view that reading newspapers and watching television news are generally a waste of time.
reviews.overall: Em đã trả lời đủ hai vế của đề, giữ quan điểm phản đối rõ ràng và triển khai Body 2 mạch lạc. Cần paraphrase thực chất ở mở bài, viết đủ chuỗi ví dụ chính trị ở Body 1 theo dàn ý và thay hai chữ viết tắt bằng tên đầy đủ trong bài luyện.

Some people say we do not need printed newspaper anymore.
To what extent do you agree or disagree with this opinion?
reviews.originalEssay:
Nowadays, online news has become increasingly popular, leading to the opinion that people no longer need printed newspapers. From my perspective, there are still some reasons to use printed newspapers, but online news is more convenient and useful in modern society.
    This situation gives people several reasons to continue using printed newspapers. Firstly, printed newspapers can provide reliable information because professional journalists and editors carefully check the content before publication. Therefore, readers may feel more confident about the accuracy of the information. In addition, printed newspapers can be useful for elderly people or those who are not familiar with modern technology. They can easily read the news without needing a smartphone, computer or Internet connection. As a result, printed newspapers can still play an important role for certain groups of people.
    By contrast, online newspapers offer several advantages over their printed counterparts. First of all, they provide access to a much wider range of information. With just a few clicks, people can read news from different countries and obtain various perspectives on the same event. Furthermore, online news can be updated immediately, allowing readers to keep up with breaking events in real time. This is particularly useful when people need important information quickly. Online newspapers are also more environmentally friendly because they do not require large amounts of paper and printing materials.
    Overall, although printed newspapers remain useful for some people, online news is generally more accessible, convenient and up-to-date. reviews.overall: Em có quan điểm rõ và phát triển được lợi ích cốt lõi của hai hình thức báo. Body 2 cần hoàn thiện lợi ích về phạm vi nguồn tin và nêu rõ giá trị của cập nhật tức thì trong tình huống diễn biến nhanh. reviews.suggestedRevision:
Nowadays, online news has become increasingly popular, leading some people to argue that printed newspapers are no longer necessary. I am firmly convinced that, although printed editions retain certain benefits, online news is the more useful source for most people in modern society.

Admittedly, printed newspapers can provide dependable information. Unlike many online platforms, they are required to follow journalistic standards and undergo careful fact-checking before publication; consequently, readers may place greater trust in their content. They also remain useful for people who lack technological awareness or access, helping them stay connected with current affairs. Nevertheless, these benefits do not prove that print itself determines accuracy or access. Many reputable news organisations publish both printed and digital editions, so the reliability of a report depends on its provider rather than its format. In addition, affordable Internet connections and smart devices are becoming more available across age groups, making online news easier to reach.

Online newspapers offer advantages that far outweigh those of their printed counterparts. With just a few clicks, readers can consult a wider range of sources, follow global events in multiple languages, and compare perspectives on the same issue—options that physical newspapers, limited by space and distribution, cannot provide. Furthermore, online platforms enable real-time updates. Through the Internet, breaking news can be reported instantly, allowing the public to access crucial information without delay; this is particularly vital during fast-developing situations such as storms or emergencies.

Overall, although printed newspapers remain useful for some people, online news is generally more accessible, convenient, and up-to-date. Therefore, I agree that printed newspapers are no longer necessary for most people in modern society.

evidence: readers may feel more confident about the accuracy of the information

criteria.comment: Chuỗi về kiểm chứng thông tin có bước giải thích hợp lý.
